knowledge.text: Under the current search edit, the Candidate reached untried location types that held the goal object in three pairs whose un-edited Parent ended at the 50-step limit: train:0030 'put a hot mug in coffeemachine' (Parent step_limit 50 vs Candidate success 25; the Candidate moved to sidetable 1 at Q1:19 and took mug 1 at Q1:20 before heating and delivering, whereas the Parent's 50 logged steps repeatedly re-entered countertop 1 and cabinet 1 and never include sidetable 1), train:0034 'find two cd and put them in drawer' (Parent step_limit vs Candidate success 15; the Candidate's first action was dresser 1 at Q5:1, where it took cd 1 at Q5:2 and cd 2 at Q5:13, whereas the Parent never selected dresser 1 and kept re-sweeping drawers/shelves), and train:0036 'find two keychain and put them in armchair' (Parent step_limit vs Candidate success 45; the Candidate reached tvstand 1 at Q7:42 and took keychain 3 at Q7:43, whereas the Parent never selected tvstand 1). These Parent-failure/Candidate-success contrasts are consistent with the edit's stall clause (prefer a destination of a location type not in recent observations once same-family instances yield nothing), but that clause constrains which destinations to avoid, not which new type to try first, so the whole-task gains are not uniquely attributable to it.

The added two-object clause ('after delivering the first found instance, resume the search sweep until the second is found and placed') left same-receptacle delivery intact in the four successful Candidate two-object runs, where both instances went to one container: train:0034 drawer 1 (Q5:5, Q5:15), train:0036 armchair 1 (Q7:6, Q7:45), train:0037 sofa 1 (Q8:6, Q8:12), and train:0038 sidetable 1 (Q9:4, Q9:11), matching the Parent's same-receptacle deliveries where it completed (P8:4/P8:13 sofa 1; P9:5/P9:14 sidetable 1). The batch's only Parent-success/Candidate-failure regression, train:0035 'put two candle in drawer' (Parent success 45 vs Candidate step_limit 50), instead arose after the Candidate located both candles on countertop 1 early (Q6:5-Q6:6, Q6:12) but placed candle 1 in drawer 3 (Q6:8) and candle 2 in drawer 5 (Q6:14), leaving the two-object goal unsatisfied, then cycled among drawers 1-8 and countertop 1 to the step limit; the Parent put both candles in the same drawer (drawer 7, P6:41 and P6:45). The immediate trigger of the regression is therefore the Candidate splitting the two instances across two containers, not a failure to find them; whether the resume-sweep clause contributed to that split is not established.

On three single-transform pairs where the object was found, the Candidate used slightly more steps than the Parent without changing the outcome: train:0031 'heat some plate and put it in cabinet' (Parent success 10 vs Candidate success 17; the Candidate detoured to cabinet 2 and revisited cabinet 1/countertop 1/countertop 2 before taking plate 3 at Q2:12, while the Parent went countertop 1 -> countertop 2 -> cabinet 1 -> countertop 3 and took plate 3 at P2:5), train:0032 'put a hot potato in fridge' (7 vs 8; the Candidate opened the closed microwave at Q3:4 before heating at Q3:5, whereas the Parent heated the held potato at the closed microwave at P3:4), and train:0033 'heat some tomato and put it in countertop' (8 vs 10; the Candidate checked countertop 1 and countertop 2 at Q4:1-Q4:2 before opening the fridge at Q4:4, while the Parent opened the fridge first at P4:1 and heated at P4:6). These step differences are consistent with the edit's open-arrived-container and untried-location guidance, but the chosen routes are not uniquely determined by the clauses.

On the examine-under-desklamp pair val:0000 ('look at alarmclock under the desklamp') the Parent and Candidate used identical three-action sequences — go to desk 1 (P10:1 / Q10:1), take alarmclock 2 (P10:2 / Q10:2), use desklamp 1 (P10:3 / Q10:3) — and both succeeded, so the current search edit left this direct examine flow unchanged.

The current edit's anti-revisit/stall clause did not remove repeated visits in Candidate runs: on train:0030 the Candidate re-entered countertop 1 (Q1:8, Q1:12, Q1:17) and cabinet 1 (Q1:14, Q1:18) before reaching the target; on train:0036 it cycled among coffeetable 1, sidetable 1, sidetable 2 and drawers 1-2 for most of the episode (e.g., Q7:10, Q7:11, Q7:14, Q7:15, Q7:20, Q7:26, Q7:30) before finally reaching tvstand 1 at Q7:42; and on train:0035 it cycled drawers 1-8 and countertop 1 (e.g., Q6:19, Q6:23, Q6:34, Q6:38, Q6:47, Q6:50). Because the Actor sees only the current observation, the admissible actions and the last two pre-action observation/action pairs and keeps no persistent notes, whether the clause was ignored or was simply too narrow (its 'last one or two observed steps' window) to suppress longer cycles cannot be separated.
